7.3.4.3 Data Communication Graphs involving NvBlockSwComponents
In the special case of non volatile data the RIPS FlatInstanceDescriptor will reference the AbstractProvidedPortPrototype of the NvBlockSwComponent. As the protection and buffering always has to consider the complete Data Communication Graph and this Data Communication Graph in this case not only includes the direction from the data element of the ramBlock to the consuming software component, but also from the producing software component to the data element in the ramBlock, this single RIPS FlatInstanceDescriptor also affects the latter connection.
[SWS_Rte_80033] Upstream requirements: SRS_Rte_00300, SRS_Rte_00301
⌈The RTE Generator and the RTE Implementation Plug-In shall consider all VariableDataPrototype instances in PortPrototypes of Atomic Software Components which are connected to VariableDataPrototype instances in PortPrototypes of the NvBlockSwComponent which in turn are mapped together with the same NvBlockDataMapping to an element of the ramBlock as belonging to the same Data Communication Graph. Additionally the mapped element of the ramBlock belongs to this Data Communication Graph.⌋ The RTE Generator can use the fact of [SWS_NvM_00347] that all ramBlock accesses within a NvBlockSwComponent are done in the call context of the ExecutableEntity NvM_MainFunction. Figure 7.9: Data Communication Graph involving a NvBlockSwComponent The figure 7.9 illustrates an example for a Data Communication Graph involving a NvBlockSwComponent. Thereby the RIPS FlatInstanceDescriptor MyNvData1 is referencing the p-port ppNvDat1 of the NvBlockSwComponent myN- vBlockSwc. This enables the RTE Implementation Plug-In also for the partial Data Communication Graph from the p-port ppNvDat1 of the Atomic Software Component myComponent to the r-port rpNvDat1 of the NvBlockSwComponent.
